answer: A proposed auditor makes each key precommit a salt-encoded 96-GiB cache of glacier and juniper observations. At a random shared instant auditors whisper 64 indices; validators check Merkle proofs against that key’s root within two seconds. A farm can share its model and rent servers, but encoding ties the cache to one key: rebuilding 64 random blocks from a common source misses the deadline. Each clone must reserve another live 96 GiB throughout the epoch, even on rented RAM. A missing or false proof forfeits that key’s pending pay; validators enforce this, not MinePoA today.
